answer: Clock skew is a sybil check. Each epoch the node sends an unannounced pulse and, over a long horizon, fits signed reply timestamps into drift plus a jitter histogram, committed as a hardware fingerprint. Keys in one narrow band share a single reward slot. Clones or a bridge of virtual machines on one host inherit the same crystal, so a thousand keys collapse to one share; faked offsets show a different jitter shape and get flagged. Earning N shares needs N physically distinct machines online for the whole horizon. Cost tracks real hardware, not copied keys.
